name: 21194-longctxdecode128-granite4tiny-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
architecture: GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM: 40 layers (36 mamba2, 4 attention), hidden 1536, 62 experts with 6 active, ~7B total and ~1B active per token, bf16.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, bounded at 24 requests / 900 s safety, first 25% of completions discarded as warmup.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, prompt exactly 31500 tokens and output exactly 128 (min = max, so the backend forces ignore_eos). Prefix caching off. Prompts are random words put through the chat template, so the engine's own prompt-token count reads somewhat above 31500; max-model-len 32768 leaves room for it.
purpose: A single-user document analyst reading 30,000-word briefs and writing short answers from a compact mixture-of-experts model on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line at commit 9f414a12adb991d04d2adf0b80f1f115d6281fad
# (v0.9.2rc1-363-g9f414a12adb9). Interpreter and hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml.
#
# The attention backend is NOT an engine argument on this engine: there is no
# `attention-backend` field in AsyncEngineArgs here, so it is set through
# VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND in configs/tuned.yaml.

model: ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 32768
# Pinned rather than left to resolve: reached through `AsyncLLMEngine.from_engine_args` these
# fall back to the scheduler's own 2048 / 128 instead of the values this setup declares.
max-num-batched-tokens: 16384
max-num-seqs: 1024
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: false
enforce-eager: true
